question: Did the EXP-06 proof budget expire in the test harness before the optimized verifier ran, and does the 7821-byte vm.etch literal explain that delay?

savedExp06Graph.program: byte-identical to the optimized test harness runtime
savedExp06Graph.conclusion: The saved execution had not entered the target verifier runtime. This alone does not identify the cause of slow execution.

comparison.environment: Pinned Kontrol/KEVM image and generic K definition from EXP-06; same test shape, solc 0.4.19, optimizer 200 runs, BYZANTIUM, no gas proof
comparison.setupObservation: Kore definition serialization finished successfully in 10.221 seconds before either 90-second proof budget began. Both Kontrol processes selected the test function and reported that they were running the test function. Neither saved a proof graph before termination, so the records cannot separate later claim initialization from symbolic execution work.
comparison.difference: The large case embeds the exact EXP-06 7821-byte verifier runtime; the stub case substitutes the 5-byte runtime 60006000fd. The stub has no verifier semantics.
comparison.conclusion: Both bounded runs timed out after claim selection but before saving a proof graph. This comparison cannot establish whether the large literal is the bottleneck; shared claim preparation or symbolic execution may dominate.

designImplication: Kontrol can prove small library properties as in EXP-05, but this attempt still does not establish that it can prove a property of the exact optimized verifier runtime. Keep that formal-feasibility question open when selecting the design; do not count these attempts as FV-03/FV-04 proofs.
scopeLimit: No verifier correctness, cryptographic soundness, gas bound, or PoC implementation is established. No full-verifier proof was attempted.
